Wellington School required additional classroom accommodation to provide increased capacity for examinations and teaching.

SiBCAS was appointed to manufacture, deliver and install a new modular classroom facility, providing the school with a high-quality, flexible space within a tight project timeframe.
90' x 32' Triple Classroom / Exam Hall
Classroom and examination space

The key challenge was the programme, with the main installation required to take place during the school’s October break to minimise disruption to pupils and staff.

The final week of the project also had to be completed while the school was operational, requiring careful planning and coordination to ensure work could continue safely and efficiently alongside day-to-day school activities.

SiBCAS designed and manufactured a modular classroom facility tailored to Wellington School’s requirements.

The building was manufactured off-site, allowing SiBCAS to maintain quality control while reducing the amount of work required within the live school environment. Once complete, the modular units were transported to site and installed within the planned programme, creating a spacious and flexible environment suitable for both classroom teaching and examinations.

The new modular facility was successfully delivered and installed within the required timeframe and completed to a high standard.

Any final items identified ahead of handover were addressed promptly, providing Wellington School with the additional space it required and a flexible facility that can support both teaching and examination requirements.

title: The Hamilton Park Racecourse Company Ltd
author: T D
subtitle: Hamilton Racecourse - Jockeys' canteen / Warm-up Area / Physiotherapy Room / WC & Drug Testing Room
excerpt: Hamilton Park Racecourse required a new bespoke modular facility to support updated British Horseracing Authority standards for jockey welfare. With space within the existing Weighing Room limited, SiBCAS was appointed…

blocks.html:
Hamilton Park Racecourse required a new bespoke modular facility to support updated British Horseracing Authority standards for jockey welfare.

With space within the existing Weighing Room limited, SiBCAS was appointed to supply and install a new Permaspace facility incorporating a jockeys’ canteen, warm-up area, physiotherapy room, WC and drug testing room. The project also included site investigations, local authority approvals, foundations, drainage, service enabling works, ramps and steps.
40' x 10' Perma linked to a 24' x 16' Permaspace facility
Hamilton Racecourse - Jockey's canteen / Warm-up Area / Physiotherapy Room / WC & Drug Testing Room

A key challenge was maximising the available footprint adjacent to the existing Weighing Room while maintaining essential circulation space around the facility.

The programme was also critical, with site works commencing in early March and the completed facility required ahead of Hamilton Park’s new racing season. Careful planning and coordination were therefore essential to ensure the building was delivered, installed and fully operational within the required timeframe.

SiBCAS delivered a bespoke modular solution designed around the available space and the specific welfare requirements of Hamilton Park’s jockeys.

During the project, the specification for the access ramp and steps was changed from a prefabricated steel system to an in-situ concrete and powder-coated steel solution. This provided a successful alternative that met the requirements of the facility and offers a solution that could be adopted on future projects.

The new facility was successfully completed on time and on budget, providing Hamilton Park with a modern, dedicated environment designed to support jockey welfare.

As well as providing enhanced facilities on racedays, the flexible space can be used by the Hamilton Park team throughout the year, adding longer-term value beyond its primary function.

“Delivered on time and on budget, the unit also serves as a versatile space for our team on non-racedays. We are incredibly grateful to the SiBCAS team for their hard
work in delivering an exceptional facility that will support jockey welfare at Hamilton Park Racecourse, for years to come.”

Stuart Heywood
Operations & Experience Manager
The Hamilton Park Racecourse Company Ltd

title: Secondary School – Wolverhampton
author: T D
subtitle: Secondary School - Wolverhampton
excerpt: Design, supply, and install a two-storey modular building complex to enable the construction team to demolish and rebuild part of the main school. The temporary building needed to include all necessary teaching rooms,…

blocks.html: Design, supply, and install a two-storey modular building complex to enable the construction team to demolish and rebuild part of the main school. The temporary building needed to include all necessary teaching rooms, staff offices, and toilet facilities to support the normal school curriculum.
26 Classrooms comprising of 106 modules

One of the primary challenges was to keep the client’s costs to a minimum while reducing the reinstatement time. SiBCAS provided an innovative surface-mounted concrete plank solution that could be installed quickly. This method, which involved surface mounting onto the client’s prepared stone base, eliminated the need for below ground excavations when the buildings were removed. Additionally, due to the wide curriculum being taught in the modular buildings, there was a need for the construction team to provide a high level of furniture, fixtures, and equipment (F,F&E). SiBCAS worked closely with the client and their F,F&E installer from the design phase through to the installation of the furniture and equipment in the specialist teaching areas.

The modular building was designed to accommodate secondary school pupils and met the Department for Education (DfE) and Building Regulation standards. It was built to withstand daily use by over 700 students. The curriculum that was to be covered in the 26 classrooms included a wide range of subjects such as IT, Graphics, Food Technology, Construction Textiles, Resistant Materials Workshop, and Art & Technology. This comprehensive approach ensured that all educational needs were met within the temporary facility. SiBCAS were able to deliver the 26 classrooms, including staff offices, SEN Group facilities, prep stores, hygiene room, plant room, server room, internal stairwells and external ramp and step access comprising of 106 modules, within an impressive 20-week period.

The project was successfully completed, and the buildings were handed over to the client. The school was able to occupy the new facilities in time for the pupils’ return after their Easter break. This ensured minimal disruption to the students’ education and allowed the construction team to proceed with the demolition and rebuilding of the main school.

title: Xaverian College
author: T D
subtitle: Xaverian College - Classroom Facilities
excerpt: The St Edwards site at Xaverian College required 10 temporary classrooms during the works to upgrade the College Campus with a new build Sunbury building. The brief was to provide a bespoke L-shaped layout to suit the…

blocks.html: The St Edwards site at Xaverian College required 10 temporary classrooms during the works to upgrade the College Campus with a new build Sunbury building. The brief was to provide a bespoke L-shaped layout to suit the available plot of land.
12 on 12 9.75m x 3m two storey classroom block with internal staircase.

The project presented several challenges:

  • Coordination with Other Contractors: SiBCAS had to work in conjunction with various other contractors engaged in the demolition of an existing church building, which was partially on the footprint of the modular location.
  • Groundworks: Extensive new groundworks were required under the building to provide a new Storm Bloc storage tank and Oil Separator tank.
  • Site Conditions: The site was considerably sloping, and there was an old boundary wall in poor condition. These factors necessitated multiple changes to the exact location of the building.
  • Installation Constraints: The installation required the use of a 150-ton crane and a specialist LMC to install the building in a highly restrictive area. Access to the site was also very restrictive, requiring extensive work to minimise damage to the ornamental gate posts.

SiBCAS designed and delivered a custom modular building solution that met the specific requirements of the Xaverian College project. The bespoke L-shaped layout was carefully planned to fit the available plot of land. The two-storey classroom block was constructed with an internal staircase, providing a functional and efficient space for the college during the upgrade works.

Despite the challenges and resulting delays, SiBCAS successfully handed over a high-quality building. The temporary classrooms provided an environment that met the highest possible standards expected of such an outstanding and prestigious institution. The project was completed to the satisfaction of all parties involved, demonstrating SiBCAS's ability to deliver complex modular building solutions in challenging conditions.

From the start of the procurement process, through to installation, SiBCAS provided a professional service and ensured we were kept up to date with the progress of the project and the timelines for ground prep, delivery etc. They listened to the specification requirements for our temporary accommodation and delivered on that specification. When we later tweaked our requirements, they were agile and could accommodate these changes with minimal fuss.

- Ivan Lewis, Financial Director

blocks.html: Celtic Football Club, one of Scotland’s most prestigious football teams, required a bespoke media room at their Lennoxtown training ground. The facility would accommodate press conferences, player interviews, and other media-related activities, enhancing the club’s content production capabilities and allowing them to produce high-quality digital content for fan engagement and filming.

SiBCAS provided two customised SiBCAS CTX modules specifically designed for media production. These units were delivered and installed within six weeks. To optimise the space for media activities, the units featured:

  • Low-profile heaters: These were installed to maximise wall space and remain out of view during filming, ensuring the aesthetic appeal of the room and allowing greater flexibility for camera placement.
  • Custom external finish: To align with the club’s branding, SiBCAS adjusted the colour of its logo on the units to green and white, reflecting Celtic’s iconic identity.

The media room was completed within the six-week schedule and is now fully operational. The bespoke low-profile heaters have maximised usable wall space, ensuring that filming operations are not hindered by bulky equipment while keeping the room comfortably heated. This new media facility has significantly enhanced Celtic Football Club’s ability to produce professional-quality content, such as live broadcasts and interviews, further strengthening their engagement with fans and media outlets. The units, with their green and white branding, have seamlessly integrated into the club’s existing facilities.

All units were built and installed to meet the highest safety and quality standards.

SiBCAS Ltd. Offers Support Amidst Widespread Building Concerns

In light of the growing concerns due to the alarming discoveries surrounding Reinforced Autoclaved Aerated Concrete (RAAC) in UK public buildings, SiBCAS Ltd., with over 50 years of experience in the education sector, is ramping up its efforts to address the increasing demand for temporary accommodations.

Recognising the profound implications of these recent findings, SiBCAS remains committed to delivering essential support to affected communities. Our modular building solutions offer an adaptable, high-quality, and immediate remedy to the pressing needs.

What is RAAC?

RAAC, a once-popular lightweight building material, was extensively used in regions like the UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, and South Africa from the 1950s to the mid-1990s. Initially hailed for its affordability and ease of installation, later evaluations raised concerns over its durability.

It’s now understood to be susceptible to collapse when exposed to moisture. It has an estimated lifespan of only about 30 years. This widespread usage poses a challenge extending beyond schools, reaching as far as hospitals, housing blocks, airports, theatres, and other public buildings.

The RAAC Controversy in the UK

Incidents like the roof collapse at Singlewell Primary School in Kent have thrown the RAAC issues into sharp relief. The severity of the situation is underscored by the revelation that over 174 schools have been currently identified as having RAAC-related concerns. This has resulted in schools adopting various measures like hybrid learning models and temporary classroom accommodations. However, the problem goes beyond educational institutions. RAAC is being identified in many public buildings across the UK, with venues such as the Motherwell Concert Hall and Theatre who have had to shut their doors because of RAAC.

SiBCAS Ltd. Responds

More than just a modular building provider, SiBCAS Ltd. is a family business deeply embedded in the education sector. Recognising the acute demand for temporary facilities, SiBCAS has an array of high-quality, relocatable modular classrooms available for hire and purchase. These solutions, manufactured off-site in purpose-built factories, ensure minimal disruption to school activities. Furthermore, with an expansive fleet of commercial vehicles, SiBCAS guarantees prompt delivery and seamless removal when these classrooms are no longer essential.

The SiBCAS modular classrooms are tailored to meet educational standards, are versatile and can be customised to exact specifications, ensuring a conducive learning atmosphere for students of all ages. The objective goes beyond merely providing space; it’s about restoring confidence and ensuring educational continuity for teachers and pupils in affected establishments.

SiBCAS Ltd. remains at the forefront as this situation unfolds, assisting local authorities and schools through these daunting times with prompt, modular solutions. Trusted collaborations, like the one presented by SiBCAS, are indispensable during such uncertain times.

In order to better co-ordinate the demolition and rebuild of the medical centre, Sibcas also carried out enabling works to the main site. This was to allow the main construction company, responsible for the rebuild, to begin works without impeding the day to day operation of the Sibcas medical facility.

• Provision of fully equipped consulting rooms.
  • Accommodation for all medical staff, district nurses, locums, visiting staff.
  • Sufficient capacity to replicate the services being provided by the exisiting Silsden Medical Practice

Success in the RoSPA Awards 2013 for SiBCAS Ltd

SiBCAS Ltd has had its approach to occupational safety and health recognised in an awards scheme run by the safety charity, the Royal Society for the Prevention of Accidents (RoSPA).

The Silver award has been presented as part of the RoSPA Occupational Health and Safety Awards 2013.

David Rawlins, RoSPA’s awards manager, said: “RoSPA firmly believes that organisations that demonstrate commitment to continuous improvement in accident and ill health prevention deserve recognition. SiBCAS Ltd has shown that it is committed to striving for such continuous improvement and we are delighted to honour it through the presentation of an award.”
